the decision interval: squadopt.evaluation.statistics.season_aware_moving_block_interval over decision_level_reading.interval_inputs with decision_level_reading.interval_candidate_id

R2.clause: 2025-26 paired interval (control minus candidate) entirely above zero

R3.clause: 2024-25 paired interval not entirely below zero

D1.clause: decision-level paired mean, candidate minus linear, at or above zero

phase_c_component_oof_development_v2_equ.chronology_check: training_cutoff_utc < decision_timestamp_utc is unrunnable on archive folds: neither timestamp is published and neither may be forged. The substitute is stronger because it reads the set rather than a boundary -- for every fold, fold_id is absent from training_fold_ids and every training fold ranks before it under development_seasons order. The export enforces both and refuses rather than recording a violation. training_cutoff_fold_id is the ordinal analogue of training_cutoff_utc, and training_key_digest covers the training row set rather than only its fold labels.
phase_c_component_oof_development_v2_equ.decision_timestamp_policy: The archive publishes no deadline and one cannot be recovered from a kickoff time, so decision_timestamp_utc is missing on every row. What guarantees these rows is structural: every feature is a shift(1) rolling aggregate or a declared pre-match column, each fold trains strictly before its own gameweek, and no outcome column is in the feature set.
phase_c_component_oof_development_v2_equ.development_note: Phase C v2 development path. 2025-26 is read here as development data under this separate contract; the repository has used that season before, so nothing measured on it is an unseen final test. The v1 contract, its artifacts and its refusals are unchanged, and this artifact is not binding evidence for any later phase.

estimator.name: linear
estimator.rule: standardized logistic regression (appearance) and ridge regression (minutes and points given an appearance), the control

phase_c_component_oof_development_v2_equ.missing_data_policy: A missing value is missing. Conditional targets are absent where the player did not appear; a row without complete features takes the direct_control route and carries no component prediction; the start component is unavailable, not zero. Nothing is imputed.
phase_c_component_oof_development_v2_equ.public_points_bound: control_expected_points = max(0, appearance_probability * raw_expected_points_if_appearance), both factors read at the exported precision
phase_c_component_oof_development_v2_equ.public_points_bound_note: Equivalent to clipping the conditional first, because a probability is non-negative. The two derived columns are composed from the *rounded* independent columns, so a reader recomputing them from the file gets the value the file carries; deriving them from unrounded inputs left a discrepancy of 4.4e-09 with only 201 of 100,130 rows exact.
phase_c_component_oof_development_v2_equ.reproduce: This artifact reads only the pinned public archive, so it can be rebuilt rather than transferred: python -m scripts.fetch_historical_data (verifies against the committed checksum manifest), then python -m scripts.export_component_oof --development-scope v2 --season-weighting equal, at the repository_commit below. Byte-identical output is the check -- compare table_sha256 and roster_sha256. Only generated_at_utc differs between runs.
phase_c_component_oof_development_v2_equ.roster_ownership_policy: Omitted. selected_by_percent is the only ownership column the panel carries and data/schema.py classifies it in AMBIGUOUS_TIMING_COLUMNS, so its snapshot timing cannot be proven -- it fails the 'only if timing is verified' condition rather than passing it quietly.

rule_era.note: 2025-26 total_points already include the defensive-contribution points introduced that season, so points_target embeds the new scoring era for 2025-26 rows while 2021-22..2024-25 were scored without it. No defensive-action column enters the panel, the features or the targets; nothing is added, re-thresholded or imputed, and an absent action count in an earlier season is absent, not a measured zero.

weighting.normalization: mean 1 within each fitted subset -- complete-feature rows for the appearance model, appeared rows with both conditional targets for the minutes and points models -- and the same weights are passed to the StandardScaler and to the estimator of each pipeline

constants.gate: StandardScaler + LogisticRegression (lbfgs, C 1.0) over the regime labels
constants.rule_era: defcon for season start year 2025 or later

estimator.name: regime
estimator.rule: one linear expert set (the control's estimators and constants) per regime label, fixture regime (single, double) by rule era (pre_defcon, defcon), fitted on that regime's rows; mixed by a standardized multinomial logistic gate on the v1 features plus the regime terms (double indicator, defcon indicator, season age); an expert below the minimum rows is absent and the gate mass is renormalized; equal weighting only

comparison.acceptance_rule: The candidate is preferred only if (i) its primary-season points MAE is lower than the control's, (ii) the 90% season-aware moving-block interval of the per-fold paired differences (control MAE minus candidate MAE) on the primary season lies entirely above zero, and (iii) the same interval on the previous-era season does not lie entirely below zero. Otherwise there is no selection and the control remains the reference. No minimum effect size is imposed and none is added afterwards.

control_era_season.paired_difference_sign: control MAE minus candidate MAE; positive favours the candidate

primary_season.paired_difference_sign: control MAE minus candidate MAE; positive favours the candidate

verdict.rule: The candidate is preferred only if (i) its primary-season points MAE is lower than the control's, (ii) the 90% season-aware moving-block interval of the per-fold paired differences (control MAE minus candidate MAE) on the primary season lies entirely above zero, and (iii) the same interval on the previous-era season does not lie entirely below zero. Otherwise there is no selection and the control remains the reference. No minimum effect size is imposed and none is added afterwards.

decision_level_reading.scope: decision-level reading declared with the rule; the candidate exported at the same commit for the frozen decision seasons 2021-22 to 2024-25 and scored by scripts.evaluate_phase_c_components with --development-contract (147 folds, the ridge control of the frozen evaluation on the same folds); the linear components' reading is the one recorded beside the gradient-boosting comparison
decision_level_reading.decision_scorer_note: scripts.evaluate_phase_c_components with --development-contract is the admission of a development handoff to the frozen decision comparison, commit b344b9ca7 on branch feat/component-decision-development-arm, which was not merged and not on this branch when the arm ran (the flag does not exist at 1ec7ae20 or at the record commit); the scorer ran from that commit's checkout on this branch's exported table, as the earlier gradient-boosting records did, and both arms' decision files carry repository_commit b344b9ca7. It has since been squashed into develop as #1137 (1079ba64c).
decision_level_reading.interval_inputs: the 147 paired differences arms.regime.folds minus arms.linear.folds in ascending fold_id order, each paired with its season (the fold_id's first seven characters), under PromotionPolicy(confidence_level=0.90, bootstrap_resamples=5000, moving_block_length=4, deterministic_seed=0); the bootstrap seed is deterministic_seed plus the first eight hex digits of sha256(interval_candidate_id)
decision_level_reading.interval_reproduction_note: Added 2026-10-18, after the result, at commit 1367d4bc1. The first record did not carry the candidate_id that seeds this interval's bootstrap. decision_regime_gated_vs_linear reproduces the recorded interval exactly from interval_inputs, and so does phase_c_regime_gated_experts_vs_linear, so which id the first computation used cannot be told apart; the recorded interval is unchanged. Under the comparison's own candidate_id phase_c_v2_regime_vs_linear the same inputs give [-0.673469387755102, 1.687414965986396]. Both intervals cross zero, and D1 reads the mean only.

expert_availability.note: first walk-forward fold whose regime fit held each expert: every one of the 184 folds refitted from the archive with fit_component_models (estimator regime) and read with regime_expert_summary; every fold's training key digest equals the exported manifest's and the refused folds agree (2021-22-gw02 only). Descriptive, not a gate.
expert_availability.never_fitted_note: double_defcon never reached the minimum rows: before the last fold 2025-26 had 408 feature-complete double-gameweek rows (gameweeks 26, 33 and 36, counted from the exported table), of which 171 appeared, below the 200 conditional rows an expert needs. The 2025-26 double-gameweek rows were therefore scored by the present experts with the gate's mass on double_defcon renormalized over them

lowest_own_expert_gate_weight.note: the smallest gate weight on a scored row's own regime expert, over the feature-complete non-blank scored rows of every fold whose fit had a gate, where the row's regime had an expert

first_record_proxy.note: the first record read availability from the exported control table (first fold with at least 200 complete rows and 200 appeared rows of the regime strictly before it). That proxy cannot see the refused fold's rows: 2021-22-gw02 exported all its rows on the direct_control route, although 554 of them were the feature-complete training rows of the 2021-22-gw03 fit, so it put single_pre_defcon one fold late

points_mae_by_season_and_fixture_group.note: points MAE by fixture group and season over exactly the rows the comparison's points metric scores (scripts.compare_component_oof_development._scored_points), read from the two exported tables; the pooled values equal the recorded by_fixture_group metrics. Descriptive, not a gate.
